item.title: Taisanji Temple: A National Treasure in Kobe's Western Hills — Guide
item.description: Taisanji sits in a forested valley in Kobe’s Nishi Ward, far enough from the city that most visitors never hear of it — which is a pity, because its main hall, rebuilt in 1293 after a fire, is a designated National Treasure and one of the finest medieval buildings in the Kansai region. The wooded grounds hold a vermilion three-storey pagoda, an Important Cultural Property gate, sub-temples and a strolling garden, and the surrounding valley turns brilliant with maples in late autumn.
